title: MOSAIC core reference v0.2
body:
# MOSAIC core reference v0.2
2026-09-27 • The Oracle • C1–C13 confirmed as the current company baseline, bounded to the inspected website. See S10 and the [founder review record](/SHE/issues/SHE-2#document-open-questions).
Sources: [register](/SHE/issues/SHE-2#document-source-register). All S-numbers below resolve there.

## Status vocabulary
**Published principle** means explicitly supported by this website snapshot. C1–C13 were subsequently confirmed within the website-only scope by S10; this does not ratify every website claim. **Supporting illustration** is an educational example. **Inference** is the curator's reading. **Proposal** is new curatorial work. **Open** means unresolved. No effectiveness claim is established by this source set.

## Plain-language account
Published principle: MOSAIC helps a decision owner move from incomplete or conflicting evidence to an explainable choice. It makes the decision context, sources, assumptions, alternatives, uncertainty and reasons inspectable. Its six forms of reasoning can be revisited as gaps emerge. It supports judgement; it does not promise certainty or transfer responsibility to an automated recommendation. [S3, S4]

The six names below are transcribed from the published framework, not invented from the acronym. Definitions are curator paraphrases checked against S4's purpose, questions and outputs.

| ID | Published form | Plain-language definition and expected result | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Meaning | Specify the actual decision, its owner, available choices, desired outcome, timing, constraints and consequences, including reversibility and delay. Result: a decision statement. | S4, meaning |
| C2 | Observations | Inventory available material and distinguish direct observation, report, inference and assumption; retain origins and gaps. Result: evidence inventory with provenance and limitations. | S4, observations |
| C3 | Structure | Connect material to claims, alternatives and choices while preserving dependencies, contradictions, assumptions and uncertainty. Result: traceable relationships, not just a tidy summary. | S4, structure |
| C4 | Analysis | Examine patterns, corroboration, contradiction, sensitivity and competing explanations. Result: findings with assumptions, provenance, limits and unresolved questions. | S4, analysis |
| C5 | Interpretation | Determine how findings affect the consequences, risks and trade-offs of possible choices; identify uncertainty that could change the decision. Result: decision-relevant implications. | S4, interpretation |
| C6 | Choice | Commit to the course best supported in context, potentially including targeted inquiry when its value warrants its cost. Record rationale, rejected alternatives, residual uncertainty and reconsideration conditions. | S4, choice |

## Cross-cutting principles and boundaries
- C7: The forms are iterative; numbered stages do not require a one-way pipeline. A choice may justify inquiry; analysis may expose missing material. [S3, S4]
- C8: Preserve provenance and disagreement. Repeated reports from one origin must not silently become independent corroboration. [S4; supporting illustration S7]
- C9: Begin with the decision rather than whatever data happens to exist. Ask whether attainable information could change the choice; more information is not automatically better. [S3, S4]
- C10: Findings do not alone determine action. Consequences, constraints, values and reversibility matter. [S4; supporting illustration S8]
- C11: External analytical work supplies material to the decision layer; operational systems implement the choice. Handoff includes rationale, constraints, uncertainty and reconsideration conditions. MOSAIC also includes a form named Analysis within the decision layer. [S4]
- C12: Outcomes may later be linked to the decision record to learn which assumptions held. Preserve what was known at decision time; distinguish decision quality from outcome quality. [S4]
- C13: Human judgement and ownership remain. The website presents examples as educational simplifications. [S3, S9 and site's shared example disclaimer]

## Supporting evidence, inference and proposals
Supporting evidence here is evidence of published framework content. S6–S9 contain attempted illustrations of framing, provenance, consequences and assumption sensitivity. S10 cautions that none of the current teaching examples should be taken as entirely useful; ignore them or refer to them only loosely. None is a validation study or an observed success rate.

Inference I1: A decision record should be navigable from action back to claims and original material. This follows C3/C6/C8 and the home page's traceability instruction. This is a practical reading, not a prescribed database schema.
Inference I2: Evidence sufficiency is choice-relative: the same material may justify a small reversible step but not a major irreversible commitment. This follows S4 and the home page examples. No universal numerical threshold was located.
Proposal P1: Use a claim/source/assumption/alternative/choice register and versioned review log for company knowledge. This is the curator's implementation aid, not an added MOSAIC stage.
Proposal P2 — deferred after S10: refine examples illustrating the six stages. The existing synthetic example is retained as an unendorsed archival draft, not an official or recommended teaching application. No refinement task or testing is authorized by this record.

## Contradictions and material uncertainty
T1 — Scoring tension: S4's Structure failure mode cautions against compressing mixed evidence into one score. S7 counts signals and S9 uses weighted ordinal support. S10 confirms that these are teaching devices and no canonical scoring method is established here. Keep the examples and warning together; do not promote their arithmetic into MOSAIC doctrine.
T2 — Tie treatment: with all default S7 signals and shared provenance linked, each explanation receives one signal. The code still chooses the first sorted entry as the lead. This is a static implementation finding, not a browser test. The support counts alone do not justify preferring that explanation.
T3 — Two uses of Analysis: S4 distinguishes the analytical layer from the decision layer, while naming an internal form Analysis. Preserve both usages; S10 confirms the boundary: external analysis supplies material; MOSAIC Analysis examines structured evidence for this decision.
T4 — Status: S5 calls the framework developing. S10 now confirms C1–C13 as a bounded company baseline; the developing status and limits of this source set remain.

## Safe handoff to Chief of Staff
Explanations may use C1–C13 as the founder-confirmed, website-bounded company baseline [S10]. Ignore or only loosely refer to current examples; do not present them as approved, fully useful teaching applications. Avoid calling the framework validated, probabilistic, a rigid six-step algorithm, an automated decision-maker, or a proven product. Do not promise the 8-of-10 comprehension target has been met. Do not use example scores as a universal method.
Suggested correction for S7: show a tie when maximum counts tie and explain that equal counts do not establish equal evidential weight. Suggested correction for S9: label weights and thresholds explicitly as arbitrary educational controls. These are review findings only; no website change is authorized or made here.

## Revision record
v0.1, 2026-09-27: initial source-grounded draft, retained in document revision history (98c45f02-6493-42ea-9b18-42ba8a49ea04).
v0.2, 2026-09-27: recorded S10 founder decisions. C1–C13 wording preserved; authority limited to the inspected snapshot. Scoring and Analysis boundaries confirmed; tie finding retained. Current examples are unendorsed and refinement remains future work. No efficacy, publication or comprehension approval inferred.

title: MOSAIC glossary, worked example and FAQ v0.2
body:
# MOSAIC learning guide v0.2
2026-09-27 • Glossary grounded in the confirmed, website-bounded core reference. Existing example retained for provenance only; see S10 and the [founder review record](/SHE/issues/SHE-2#document-open-questions).
[Core reference](/SHE/issues/SHE-2#document-core-reference) • [Source register](/SHE/issues/SHE-2#document-source-register)

## Glossary
These are plain-language paraphrases, not new canonical terminology.
- Meaning: defining the decision and what matters. [S4/C1]
- Observations: recording available material and what kind of knowledge it is. [S4/C2]
- Structure: retaining the links among sources, claims, assumptions and choices. [S4/C3]
- Analysis: examining what evidence supports, challenges or leaves unresolved. [S4/C4]
- Interpretation: explaining what findings imply for the possible choices. [S4/C5]
- Choice: committing with reasons, remaining uncertainty and reconsideration conditions. [S4/C6]
- Provenance: where an item came from and the context needed to assess it. [S4, Observations/Structure]
- Assumption: something being relied on without treating it as an established observation; test its influence on the decision. [S4, Observations/Analysis; S9]
- Corroboration: support from evidence; shared-origin reports cannot automatically be treated as independent support. [S4, Analysis; S7]
- Contradiction: material pointing against another claim or explanation, which remains visible rather than being edited away. [S4, Structure/Analysis]
- Decision-sensitive uncertainty: an unresolved matter whose resolution could alter the supportable choice. [S4, Analysis/Interpretation/Choice]
- Decision record: an inspectable account linking a choice with evidence, assumptions and rationale. A storage format is not prescribed by this baseline. [S3/S4; final sentence is inference I1]
- Reconsideration condition: new evidence or a changed assumption that should prompt review of a prior choice. [S4, Choice; S8/S9]

## Archived worked example: a reversible onboarding change
**Founder disposition (S10, 2026-09-27): not endorsed as a useful teaching application.** None of the current teaching examples should be taken as entirely useful. They may be ignored or referred to loosely; refining examples for the six stages remains future work. The draft below is preserved to make the reviewed material inspectable, not to recommend its use.
**Epistemic status:** new synthetic teaching example, proposed by The Oracle. Not a historical case, measured result, or official founder example. It adapts the product/onboarding patterns in S4 and the duplicate-source lesson in S7. All dates, quantities, costs and permissions below are hypothetical.

**Assumptions:** a product lead may authorize a £500, two-day reversible interface change. Pausing the product would require a different approval. No safety-critical functionality is involved. The team has two days to decide.

1. **Meaning (C1).** Decide whether to fix onboarding, investigate measurement first, leave the interface alone, or seek approval to pause the product. The desired outcome is successful onboarding; the lead must respect the hypothetical cost and time limits.
2. **Observations (C2).** E1: a dashboard shows completion falling from 60% to 45% after release; its event definition changed on release day. E2: the weekly email repeats that dashboard. E3: in four of six hypothetical observed sessions, users cannot find the next-action button; these sessions use a separate observation record. E4: no demand study is available. A1: moving the button is reversible within a day. A2: those six sessions may reveal a problem relevant beyond those participants, but representativeness is unproven.
3. **Structure (C3).** Link E2 to E1's originating data so they count as one provenance chain. Connect the tracking change to uncertainty about the apparent decline. Connect E3 to the usability explanation, while preserving its small-sample limitation. Link A1 to the reversible-fix option. Preserve the alternatives that instrumentation, usability, demand changes, or a mixture explain the apparent decline.
4. **Analysis (C4).** E1/E2 cannot establish a comparable pre/post decline without checking the changed definition. E3 supports a local usability problem in those sessions; it does not prove population prevalence or overall causality. E4 leaves weak demand unresolved, not demonstrated. Six sessions are not converted into a calibrated probability.
5. **Interpretation (C5).** If A1 is true, the limited usability evidence can support a small reversible improvement while measurement is checked. It does not establish grounds for the much larger step of pausing the product. The distinction rests on the stipulated consequences and reversibility, not an invented confidence score.
6. **Choice (C6).** In this hypothetical scenario, authorize the limited fix within £500, assign an analyst to check event comparability, and record why immediate pause and unchanged onboarding were not selected. Owner: product lead. Review after two days using comparable measurement and new observed sessions. Reconsider immediately if rollback proves unavailable, the cost cap is exceeded, or evidence shows harm to completion.

**Sensitivity test:** if A1 is false and rollback requires a month, the justification for immediate rollout weakens. First investigate or use a safely bounded test subject to the lead's actual authority. If comparable measurements show no decline, E3 can still justify addressing observed friction, but claims about a general drop must be withdrawn. These are conditional teaching judgements, not automatic MOSAIC rules.

**Traceability check:** the dashboard supports only the reported metric; sessions support only observed friction; the choice relies explicitly on A1, authority and cost limits. The example does not claim empirical validation. It follows C1–C6, preserves provenance under C8, tests information value under C9, and links action to consequence under C10.

## FAQ
**What is MOSAIC?** A developing framework for making inspectable, defensible choices from imperfect evidence. C1–C13 are confirmed as the current baseline bounded to the inspected website; this is not empirical validation. [S3–S5, S10]
**Must I complete six stages exactly once?** No. The site describes iterative forms of reasoning, even though it numbers stages. [S3/S4]
**Does MOSAIC replace analysis?** The published model takes analytical material into decision reasoning; it also includes Analysis internally. The founder confirmed that external analysis supplies material while MOSAIC Analysis examines structured evidence for this decision. [S4, S10]
**Does it make the decision for me?** Its published aim is to support structured judgement. The complete example leaves commitment with the decision owner. [S3/S9]
**Does more evidence always improve the decision?** The published Choice questions ask whether attainable information could change the choice and warrant its cost. [S4]
**Do example scores represent probabilities?** S9 explicitly identifies its comparison as ordinal, not probabilistic. This baseline finds no universal scoring specification. [S9; inventory limitation]
**Can we call it proven?** Not from these sources. They explain and demonstrate; no efficacy study was found in the inspected set. [source register]
**Has the website met its comprehension goal?** No result is available here. The plan's target is at least eight of the same ten people both explaining it and scoring at least four of five on a quiz. Preparing material does not demonstrate that outcome. [S1/S2]

## Archived understanding checks (deferred proposal, not the website study)
These checks depend on the unendorsed example and are not an approved teaching or evaluation instrument. [S10]
Ask a reader to explain why E1 and E2 are not two independent confirmations; identify the assumption carrying the reversible-fix decision; and name evidence that would change the choice.
Expected answers: common dashboard origin; rollback/authority/cost assumptions, especially A1; comparable metrics, adverse observed effects, or loss of reversibility. A useful explanation connects evidence to the consequence of acting; recalling stage names alone is insufficient. Chief of Staff owns the formal quiz, rubric and test protocol.

## Revision record
v0.1 (e372dbc7-aecf-466a-9606-51dee766a680) remains in document history. v0.2, 2026-09-27: applies founder authority and Analysis decisions; retains invented example facts unchanged for provenance while withdrawing any recommendation to use it.

title: MOSAIC open questions and founder review v0.2

# MOSAIC open questions and founder review v0.2
2026-09-27 • The Oracle • Material uncertainty resolved or explicitly bounded.

Review package: [sources](/SHE/issues/SHE-2#document-source-register), [core reference](/SHE/issues/SHE-2#document-core-reference), [learning guide](/SHE/issues/SHE-2#document-learning-guide).

## Decision provenance (S10)
The saved human founder-review interaction `77867ccc-219e-45fa-bb19-68e122fecdd0` is answered. Answers were supplied in the authenticated continuation on 2026-09-27, superseding earlier pending-review comments. A separate responder identity and precise answer timestamp were not exposed in that continuation.

The card targeted core revision `98c45f02-6493-42ea-9b18-42ba8a49ea04` and learning-guide revision `e372dbc7-aecf-466a-9606-51dee766a680`.

### Recorded answers
Authority: “Confirm C1–C13 as the current baseline, bounded to the inspected website; no additional source is required”

Boundaries: “Confirm those boundaries; retain the tie behavior as a correction finding”
The question specified that public counts, weights and thresholds are teaching devices, with no canonical scoring method established here; external analysis supplies material while MOSAIC Analysis examines structured evidence for this decision.

Example: “None of the teaching examples should be taken as entirely useful. Part of our goal is to refine the examples that illustrate the six stages of MOSAIC in the most helpful way possible -- we are not at the point yet so can ignore (or loosely refer to) the current examples.”

## Question dispositions
| ID | Disposition | Remaining boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Q1: C1–C13 authority | Resolved: confirmed as current baseline | Limited to inspected website snapshot; not universal ratification |
| Q2: numerical examples | Resolved: illustrative devices only | No canonical scoring method established; tie finding retained |
| Q3: Analysis boundary | Resolved: supplied distinction confirmed | External analysis supplies material; internal Analysis examines structured evidence for the decision |
| Q4: source precedence | Bounded: no additional source required | No assertion about unavailable internal history or future superseding sources |
| Q5: synthetic example | Bounded, not approved as useful | Existing examples may be ignored or loosely referenced; retained draft is archival, not a recommended teaching application |

## Contradiction and correction log
- T1: scoring tension resolved for this baseline by illustrative-only boundary. Preserve S4's warning against compressing mixed evidence into one score; S7/S9 arithmetic is not doctrine.
- T2: open implementation correction finding: S7's default linked-provenance counts tie at one each, but code returns a first-listed lead. Static finding, not browser-tested. Suggested correction: display a tie and distinguish counts from evidential weight. Chief of Staff owns any website decision; no change is made here.
- T3: overlapping Analysis names now bounded by the confirmed distinction above.
- T4: developing public framework can serve as a bounded company baseline by explicit founder decision; neither completeness nor validation follows.

## Remaining open work and ownership
Example refinement remains an acknowledged future need, not a blocker to this bounded baseline and not a newly authorized task. Chief of Staff owns prioritization of future teaching/website work. The Oracle will review MOSAIC accuracy on an explicit assignment or handoff. No efficacy evidence, validated teaching example, canonical scoring method or comprehension result is established.

## Acceptance and handoff
All requested artifacts are inspectable. C1–C13 retain source mappings and unchanged definitions; original revisions and snapshot remain available. The concrete worked example and assumptions remain inspectable but explicitly unendorsed under the founder's direction. The real review interaction resolves or bounds material uncertainty. This completes the bounded baseline; downstream website work can use C1–C13 subject to these limits and its own approvals.

v0.1: initial open-question log (834c5684-d5f8-4f3c-b573-f1bdd9be1bd3), preserved in history.
v0.2: records S10 answers, their exact scope, correction finding and example-use limitation.

title: MOSAIC source register v0.2
body:
# MOSAIC source register v0.2
Prepared 2026-09-27 by The Oracle. Status: founder-confirmed baseline C1–C13, bounded to the inspected website under S10. Website content is evidence of published wording, not proof of canonical founder intent or effectiveness.

## Inventory and retrieval
The assigned workspace contained no discoverable source files. The task had no documents or attachments at inspection. A company issue search for MOSAIC returned the onboarding task, this task, and the dependent website task. The approved parent plan was inspected. This is the accessible inventory, not a claim that no other company material exists.

The web reading tool could not open the site; direct HTTPS retrieval succeeded. The HTML is a JavaScript application shell. Its asset manifest identified the content modules below. Definitions and examples were read from those modules without executing them. No visual/browser interaction test was performed. Read date for every website source: 2026-09-27. Publication dates and semantic framework version were not stated in the inspected content. Hashed asset names identify this deployment, not a founder-approved version.

| ID | Source and provenance | Version / date | What it supports |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | [Approved plan](/SHE/issues/SHE-1#document-plan), authored by Chief of Staff; approval represented in assignment context | revision 48f482bf-90b8-4db2-9cde-37910d6e9390, revision 1, 2026-09-27 | Curatorial scope, uncertainty boundaries, website dependency, comprehension target |
| S2 | [Assignment](/SHE/issues/SHE-2), Chief of Staff task with user-provided context | read 2026-09-27; no semantic version | Required deliverables, founder review gate, company purpose |
| S3 | [Home](https://groundstoact.com/), public website | HomePage-0ur-UAbn.js | Positioning, iterative reasoning, judgement remains human |
| S4 | [Framework](https://groundstoact.com/framework), public website | framework-CyqG33ax.js and FrameworkPage-DTY4FjU2.js | Six named forms, purposes, inputs, outputs, failure modes; analysis/action boundary and learning |
| S5 | [About](https://groundstoact.com/about), public website | AboutPage-CB2G555T.js | Developing-framework status and attribution to Simon G.; biographical statements are self-description, unverified |
| S6 | [Meaning + Observations](https://groundstoact.com/examples/meaning-observations), public educational example | MeaningObservationsPage-BXz3AlfL.js | Launch framing, evidence types, reversibility |
| S7 | [Structure + Analysis](https://groundstoact.com/examples/structure-analysis), public educational example | StructureAnalysisPage-0iCINfJX.js | Shared provenance, double counting; illustrative counts and tie behavior |
| S8 | [Interpretation + Choice](https://groundstoact.com/examples/interpretation-choice), public educational example | InterpretationChoicePage-DE0Zs40z.js | Consequences and assumptions alter supportable action |
| S9 | [Complete decision](https://groundstoact.com/examples/complete-decision), public educational example | CompleteDecisionPage-CdiFJCel.js | Career decision, ordinal demonstration, sensitivity and reconsideration |

## Evidence limits
S3–S9 share one website and are not independent corroboration. No empirical evaluation, peer-reviewed validation, calibrated probabilities, approved internal manual, founder revision history, or real customer case record was identified in this inventory. Educational examples demonstrate intended reasoning; they do not establish performance. The website identifies MOSAIC as developing. S10 confirms website-only authority for C1–C13 in this baseline; no additional source is required. Completeness beyond this scope is not asserted. Current examples are not endorsed as entirely useful.

The site also exposes Insights, Contact, Privacy and the examples index. Assets were retrieved through the manifest but these peripheral pages were not assessed for substantive framework claims in this baseline. No broader web search for similarly named frameworks was used: unrelated MOSAIC systems must not be conflated with this one.

## Missing source access
- Founder-approved source document, current semantic version, and prior definitions/change log: not supplied or located.
- Any internal notes, slide decks, source repository or private worked cases: not present in inspected workspace/task materials. No expanded access is requested; a supplied approved excerpt or existing authorized link can suffice.
- Evidence behind efficacy claims and any formal decision/calibration methods: not located; omit such claims until supported.
- S10 confirms C1–C13 and the illustrative-only scoring and Analysis boundaries. No broader adaptation rights or canonical scoring specification are inferred.

## Version policy (curatorial proposal)
Retain v0.1 as the inspected public-source record in document history. Record founder decisions with responder, date, interaction and exact scope, then issue v0.2 or a founder-approved v1.0. Never replace prior wording without a revision reason. Source IDs persist; new versions get new dated entries. A hash proves captured bytes, not truth, authorship or approval.
